item.text: {"facts":[{"source_id":"SRC-ad13f25cc10fe8af","start_unit":3,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"On 21 October 2023, Tshisekedi attended the Constitutional Court’s 2023–2024 judicial reopening, whose proceedings focused on electoral litigation and the application of the 2022 electoral-law reforms before the December 2023 elections.","question_ids":["4B.1","4B.4","8B.9"],"polarity":"context","period_fit":"Directly within 2023.","ruler_attribution":"Tshisekedi attended the proceeding as head of state; the electoral-law and litigation findings were presented by court and legal officials.","limitations":["The source records attendance and institutional proceedings, not whether Tshisekedi independently protected or influenced the Court’s decisions."]},{"source_id":"SRC-044f3de431ce12a2","start_unit":3,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"The source reports a February 2026 meeting in which Tshisekedi and Cyril Ramaphosa discussed regional peace, support for peace efforts in the DRC, territorial integrity, and a common African position on critical minerals emphasizing local processing, traceability, regional value chains, and equitable benefit-sharing.","question_ids":["2B.7","5B.1","5B.4"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Outside the 2023–2023 target period; not used as direct period evidence.","ruler_attribution":"The positions and commitments are attributed to Tshisekedi and Ramaphosa in the presidential account.","limitations":["The event occurred in 2026 and therefore cannot establish conduct during 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-fd8a399fcdf9d319","start_unit":2,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"In May 2023, an IPC analysis reported that 25.8 million people in the DRC faced crisis or emergency food insecurity, while 6.7 million people in North and South Kivu and Ituri faced those levels; cited causes included poor harvests, violence-driven displacement, disease, unemployment, and collapsing infrastructure.","question_ids":["6B.2","6B.6","6B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly within 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The findings were issued by the government’s IPC analysis and reported by FAO; the source does not attribute the conditions solely to Tshisekedi.","limitations":["The figures describe national and regional conditions and do not by themselves identify the ruler’s specific decisions or causal responsibility."]},{"source_id":"SRC-fd8a399fcdf9d319","start_unit":3,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"For 2023, FAO planned assistance for about 1.8 million people in crop, livestock, and fish production and reported assisting nearly half a million people with seeds and farming tools during the 2022/2023 agricultural season; WFP planned to reach 7.1 million people and used school meals and resilience programming to support food access and livelihoods.","question_ids":["6B.2","6B.6"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Directly within 2023, but describes UN agency programming rather than a clearly ruler-directed program.","ruler_attribution":"The assistance is attributed to FAO and WFP; no direct Tshisekedi decision is identified.","limitations":["This is relevant context for welfare outcomes but is not direct evidence of presidential implementation or funding."]},{"source_id":"SRC-68978c686fa9d3dd","start_unit":2,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"A 2025 Health Ministry retrospective states that free maternity care became effective in September 2023 and that more than 2.6 million women and newborns benefited within one year; it also reports construction or rehabilitation of hospitals and operationalization of structures supporting universal health coverage.","question_ids":["6B.1","6B.2","6B.3","6B.9","8B.6","8B.7"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The policy began in September 2023, but the source was published in 2025 and reports cumulative results over the following year.","ruler_attribution":"The Health Ministry identifies universal health coverage as a national priority of Tshisekedi and attributes the policy implementation to the government.","limitations":["The source is a later government retrospective and does not independently audit the beneficiary count or isolate 2023 implementation."]},{"source_id":"SRC-68978c686fa9d3dd","start_unit":3,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"The Health Ministry reported that the government established domestic financing mechanisms for universal health coverage, including a Health Promotion Tax on imports and mandatory health insurance, intended to reduce direct household payments; it cited more than 10 million people impoverished annually by such payments.","question_ids":["5B.3","6B.1","6B.2","6B.9"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Reported in 2025 with a policy history including the 2023 launch period.","ruler_attribution":"The mechanisms are attributed to the government under Tshisekedi’s national universal-health-coverage priority.","limitations":["The source does not provide 2023 collection, coverage, or expenditure results."]},{"source_id":"SRC-86c6b1ad2d5b04d8","start_unit":4,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"In a July 2023 interview, Tshisekedi identified free primary education as his greatest satisfaction, said it had enabled many children—especially girls—to return to school, and reiterated a commitment to extend free education to secondary school.","question_ids":["5B.1","6B.1","6B.2","6B.3","8B.1"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Directly within 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The policy claims, reported benefits, and future commitment are direct statements by Tshisekedi.","limitations":["The source provides no independent enrollment, quality, financing, or implementation verification."]},{"source_id":"SRC-3158aa4d93d4c730","start_unit":3,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"At his January 2024 inauguration after reelection, Tshisekedi swore before the Constitutional Court to defend the Constitution and laws, preserve territorial integrity and national unity, and act in the general interest and respect for human rights; he announced six priorities including jobs, purchasing power, security, economic diversification, basic services, and more effective public services.","question_ids":["4B.8","8B.1","8B.9"],"polarity":"context","period_fit":"Outside the target period, occurring in January 2024; relevant only as immediate post-period continuity evidence.","ruler_attribution":"The oath and six stated priorities are attributed directly to Tshisekedi.","limitations":["The source does not establish implementation during 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-0d5545f487d8f937","start_unit":2,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"In September 2023, the IPC reported that more than 25 million people in the DRC faced crisis or emergency food insecurity; more than 5.6 million people were displaced in Ituri, North Kivu, and South Kivu, while conflict and limited rural-development investment disrupted agriculture and infrastructure.","question_ids":["3B.6","3B.7","6B.2","6B.6","6B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly within 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The findings are from IPC and FAO/WFP reporting; the source does not assign sole causal responsibility to Tshisekedi.","limitations":["The report identifies structural, conflict-related, and investment causes but does not isolate presidential decisions."]},{"source_id":"SRC-0d5545f487d8f937","start_unit":2,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"In September 2023, WFP reported a USD 629.6 million funding gap over the following six months and warned that, without funding, it could scale back assistance to 3.6 million people as early as October; FAO reported an approximately USD 80 million gap for support to vulnerable farmers for the next agricultural campaign.","question_ids":["6B.6","6B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly within 2023, with projected consequences into early 2024.","ruler_attribution":"The funding gaps and operational warnings are attributed to WFP and FAO, not directly to Tshisekedi.","limitations":["The source does not specify the share of the gaps attributable to national government decisions versus donor shortfalls or conflict conditions."]},{"source_id":"SRC-d644b5213e1ecbb2","start_unit":3,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"On 11 January 2023, Tshisekedi chaired the CPVS steering committee, which approved the Council’s 2023 roadmap; the CPVS presented progress on presidential commitments, acknowledged implementation difficulties, and set July 2023 as the planned date for receiving phase-one works under the 145-territories local-development program.","question_ids":["8B.1","8B.2","8B.5","8B.8"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly within 2023.","ruler_attribution":"Tshisekedi chaired the meeting, approved the roadmap, prioritized the 145-territories program, and instructed that administrative, budgetary, and technical obstacles not block implementation.","limitations":["The report states planned milestones and acknowledged difficulties but does not verify completion or outcomes by year-end."]},{"source_id":"SRC-d644b5213e1ecbb2","start_unit":3,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"The CPVS reported that free primary education had been implemented, while universal health coverage and free maternity care were still being materialized; the coordinator explicitly acknowledged implementation difficulties.","question_ids":["6B.1","6B.2","8B.6","8B.8"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly within 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The CPVS, a presidential technical monitoring structure, attributed the commitments and implementation effort to Tshisekedi and his government.","limitations":["The source is a presidential communication and gives no independent evaluation of service quality, reach, or financing."]},{"source_id":"SRC-a55a30a56ce8c73e","start_unit":3,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"At the October 2023 judicial reopening of the Court of Cassation, the national bar requested improved conditions and remuneration for magistrates; the Prosecutor General denounced influence-peddling and called for repression of that practice and related justice offenses; the Court’s ordinary judicial activities then resumed.","question_ids":["3B.4","4B.4","7B.6"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly within 2023.","ruler_attribution":"Tshisekedi attended as the state’s senior judicial authority; judicial officials made the requests and denunciations.","limitations":["The source documents public statements and attendance, not subsequent funding, enforcement, or institutional independence outcomes."]},{"source_id":"SRC-aac1141303d7d7b3","start_unit":3,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"On 11 January 2023, the CPVS steering committee chaired by Tshisekedi approved a 2023 monitoring roadmap for presidential commitments and described the CPVS as a technical body created by ordinance to monitor, evaluate, and implement government-program commitments.","question_ids":["8B.2","8B.3","8B.5"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Directly within 2023.","ruler_attribution":"Tshisekedi chaired the committee and the CPVS operated as a presidential monitoring and implementation structure.","limitations":["This source duplicates the substantive account in SRC-d644b5213e1ecbb2; it is retained as a separate document but adds no independent outcome evidence."]},{"source_id":"SRC-46671b8eb3a44c65","start_unit":3,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"On 25 June 2023, Tshisekedi publicly called for cooperation between the state and the Catholic Church, said the Church should promote love, unity, and equality, and stated that he would not accept a divisive trend.","question_ids":["3B.3","3B.9","4B.3","4B.7"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Directly within 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The statements were delivered directly by Tshisekedi at a public event in Mbuji-Mayi.","limitations":["The source records rhetoric, not a specific legal, administrative, or enforcement action."]},{"source_id":"SRC-46671b8eb3a44c65","start_unit":3,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"At the same June 2023 event, Tshisekedi gave a new all-terrain vehicle to Catholic Bishop Bernard Kasanda for pastoral travel.","question_ids":["7B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly within 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The presidential account states that Tshisekedi personally delivered the vehicle.","limitations":["The source does not disclose the vehicle’s value, procurement process, funding source, or whether the gift created a conflict of interest."]},{"source_id":"SRC-ebf1723433d397f8","start_unit":3,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"In September 2022, the government submitted a proposed 2023 budget of USD 14.6 billion, approximately 32% above the prior year; the proposal identified the 145-territories development program and timely 2023 elections as priorities and was submitted within the constitutional deadline.","question_ids":["4B.1","5B.1","5B.3","5B.6","8B.2","8B.3"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The proposal was made in 2022 for execution in 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The budget priorities are described as being carried by Tshisekedi’s presidential program, while the formal submission was made by Prime Minister Sama Lukonde.","limitations":["This is a proposed rather than executed budget; the source does not establish final appropriations, spending, or results during 2023."]}],"documents_with_no_material_fact":["SRC-044f3de431ce12a2","SRC-3158aa4d93d4c730"],"batch_limitations":["The supplied corpus is dominated by official government or presidential communications and humanitarian agency reports; it contains limited independent scrutiny of presidential conduct, implementation quality, accountability, or causal responsibility.","Several documents fall outside the 2023–2023 target period or provide retrospective reporting; these are explicitly marked with period-fit limitations."]}
